Fix for "cache.backends.db._cull sometimes fails with 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable".

Root cause: In `DatabaseCache._cull`, the entry count (COUNT(*)) and the culling-key lookup are separate statements. When the rows counted earlier no longer exist by the time `cache_key_culling_sql()` runs (another process cleared the temporary/test cache table), the SELECT returns no row, so `cursor.fetchone()[0]` raised "'NoneType' object is not subscriptable" out of `set()`/`_base_set`.

Change (django/core/cache/backends/db.py): fetch the culling row into a variable first and return early when it is None, since there is then nothing to cull; otherwise use the fetched key in the DELETE.

Verification on this exact version (v2, files_sha256 fa9eda996f...): public Django frontend, `cache.tests.DBCacheTests` — 56 collected, 56 passed, 0 failed/errors/skipped, report test-report-aa4543ab68dddee00801a829. Existing culling behavior tests (test_cull, test_zero_cull, test_second_call_doesnt_crash) still pass, confirming normal culling is unchanged.

Changed files: django/core/cache/backends/db.py (patch-1). Public pass is not hidden acceptance.

ORDER BY cache_key LIMIT 1 OFFSET cull_num), that SELECT returns no row, and the original `[cursor.fetchone()[0]]` raised TypeError out of set(). The code now fetches the row first and returns early when it is None (nothing left to cull); otherwise it passes the fetched key to the DELETE. Normal culling is unchanged.
